The activity affects card C00348-K1 belonging to customer C00348 as well as 11 other customers' cards that have no prior micro-charge habits. It was uncovered after customer C00348 disputed transaction 3660250 for $4.05, leading to an alert that connected six low-value transactions totaling $23.17 across regions 264 and 325.

case.summary: This alert was opened after customer C00348 disputed online transaction 3660250 for $4.05 on card C00348-K1. Key findings indicate that card C00348-K1 incurred 6 online charges of $2.10 to $5.08 within 21.2 days, each under $10, with no larger purchase following them and 0 such charges in the prior 90 days. Furthermore, this slow micro-charge shape appeared across 11 other customers' cards with no micro-charge habit during the 30 days up to 2017-01-28, compared to 1.0 per 30 days over the prior 3 windows. The case verdict is fraud with a fraud probability of 0.95. Final actions are to block the card, create a case, file a report, monitor connected cards, and escalate to an analyst.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report relates to unauthorized card activity identified on customer C00348's mastercard debit card, C00348-K1, involving case HHF-005. Between 2017-01-07 and 2017-01-28, an unauthorized party processed six online micro-charges totaling $23.17 on the card. The activity took place via the online channel under product code C across billing regions 264 and 325, with no device information recorded. The individual transactions included transaction 3660245 for $4.30 on 2017-01-07 at 15:32, transaction 3660246 for $5.08 on 2017-01-15 at 22:51, transaction 3660247 for $2.70 on 2017-01-16 at 14:04, transaction 3660248 for $4.94 on 2017-01-18 at 19:30, transaction 3660249 for $2.10 on 2017-01-20 at 11:03, and flagged transaction 3660250 for $4.05 on 2017-01-28 at 20:45. The cardholder reported the disputed transaction to the bank and denied making it. The unauthorized scheme was executed using small online charges of a few dollars spread over several weeks, which were never followed by a larger purchase. This specific pattern matches none of the documented fraud typologies. The identical slow micro-charge pattern was observed across 11 other customer cards during the same timeframe, including C00129-K1, C01326-K2, C01525-K2, C02851-K2, C04528-K1, C05083-K1, C06139-K2, and C09471-K2. Card C00348-K1 was blocked, the related cards were placed on monitoring, and the matter has been escalated for further analysis.
